title: 1.4 Terabytes a Day
fact: NASA's Roman Space Telescope sends home 1.4 terabytes of data a day, the most of any NASA astrophysics mission so far.
source_name: NASA, Roman launch release

title: 150 Times Safer
fact: ESA's first-of-its-kind assisted reentry of the Aeolus satellite cut the already low risk from falling debris by a factor of 150.
source_name: ESA, Final images before Aeolus demise

title: 49 Flybys of an Ocean Moon
fact: NASA's Europa Clipper will travel 1.8 billion miles to Jupiter and fly past the ocean moon Europa 49 times.
source_name: NASA, Europa Clipper

title: A Coronagraph That Never Blinks
fact: GOES-19's CCOR-1 is the world's first operational space-based coronagraph, imaging the Sun's faint corona every 15 minutes.
source_name: NOAA SWPC, CCOR-1 coronagraph

title: A Desert Feeds a Rainforest
fact: About 27.7 million tons of Saharan dust fall on the Amazon each year, enough to fill 104,908 semi trucks.
source_name: NASA, Saharan dust feeds the Amazon

title: A Dozen Photons Come Home
fact: ICESat-2's laser fires 10,000 pulses a second, each with about 300 trillion photons, and only about a dozen return to the satellite.
source_name: NASA, ICESat-2

title: A Forest That Makes Rain
fact: Amazon trees start their own rainy season two to three months before the ocean-driven rains arrive.
source_name: NASA JPL, the Amazon makes its own rainy season

title: A Half-Hour Warning From a Million Miles
fact: From about a million miles toward the Sun, NASA's IMAP can give astronauts and spacecraft near Earth about a half hour's warning of incoming radiation.
source_name: NASA, IMAP mission

title: A Million Lakes From Orbit
fact: NASA–CNES SWOT keeps watch on the water levels of more than a million lakes larger than 15 acres.
source_name: NASA Earthdata, SWOT data release

title: A Quarter-Million Corals Replanted
fact: Coral Restoration Foundation had returned 253,833 nursery-grown corals to Florida's reefs by the end of 2024 (organization figure).
source_name: Coral Restoration Foundation, 2024 annual report (organization figure)

title: A Satellite Made of Wood
fact: LignoSat, the world's first wooden satellite, was built from magnolia wood panels joined with a traditional Japanese technique that uses no glue or nails.
source_name: NASA, JAXA’s first wooden satellite deploys

title: Beavers Double the Fish
fact: In Bridge Creek, Oregon, beaver dams helped young steelhead survival jump 52% and production rise 175%.
source_name: NOAA Fisheries, Oregon beavers engineer better fish habitat

title: Closer Than Our Satellites
fact: On April 13, 2029, asteroid Apophis will pass about 20,000 miles from Earth, closer than many geosynchronous satellites.
source_name: NASA, Asteroid Apophis

title: Clouds in Motion
fact: EarthCARE carries the first cloud radar in space that can measure how fast cloud particles move up and down.
source_name: JAXA, EarthCARE Cloud Profiling Radar

title: Coastal Bodyguards
fact: There are about 80 species of mangrove trees, and their tangled roots help shield coastlines from storm surges.
source_name: NOAA, What is a mangrove forest?

title: Earth's Ultraviolet Halo
fact: Earth wears a faint ultraviolet halo, the geocorona, first photographed from the Moon by Apollo 16 in 1972; NASA's Carruthers mission now charts it from a million miles away.
source_name: NASA, Carruthers Geocorona Observatory

title: Eighteen Inches a Day
fact: In ideal conditions, kelp can grow up to 18 inches in a single day.
source_name: NOAA, What is a kelp forest?

title: Every Other Breath
fact: About half of Earth's oxygen comes from the ocean, most of it made by tiny phytoplankton.
source_name: NOAA, How much oxygen comes from the ocean?

title: Farthest Humans Have Gone
fact: The Artemis II crew reached 252,756 miles from Earth on April 6, 2026, the farthest humans have ever traveled.
source_name: NASA, Artemis II crew back on Earth

title: Five Hundred Tons a Year
fact: Baltimore's four Trash Wheels collect about 500 tons of trash and debris from the harbor each year (organization figure).
source_name: Mr. Trash Wheel, trash interception (organization figure)

title: Nursery of the Coast
fact: Salt marshes are food, refuge or nursery habitat for more than 75% of fisheries species, including shrimp and blue crab.
source_name: NOAA Ocean Service, What is a salt marsh?

title: One Thousand Rivers
fact: About 1,000 rivers contribute most riverine plastic reaching the ocean, per a Science Advances riverine-plastic study.
source_name: Meijer et al., Science Advances 2021

title: Room For 1,300 Earths
fact: You could fit roughly 1,300 Earths inside Jupiter (about 1,321 by volume).
source_name: NASA Jupiter Fact Sheet

title: Sixty-Five Million Kilograms
fact: The Ocean Cleanup reported 65 million kilograms of plastic removed as of October 2026 — their biggest year ever was 2025, with 27 million kilograms alone.
source_name: The Ocean Cleanup

title: Small Meadows, Big Carbon
fact: Seagrass covers just 0.1% of the world's seafloor but stores 11% of the organic carbon buried in the ocean.
source_name: NOAA, Blue carbon fast facts

title: The Moon Keeps Our Seasons Steady
fact: Earth's 23.5-degree tilt is kept in check by the Moon; without it, Earth could wobble more violently, drastically altering the climate.
source_name: NASA, 10 things we learn about Earth from the Moon
